=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter
Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of
Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and
look forward to your mark-up.
SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)
Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims
is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.
Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and
only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the
basket is recoverable.
Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after
Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims
unless expressly stated otherwise.
Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same
caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.
Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and
non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.
Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public
registers (see Disclosure Letter).
Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the
Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or
public records.
Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller
will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the
counterparty's written consent.
Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding)
will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.
Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing
bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds
flow.)
Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio
matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.
Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter
and is not expected to be material.
Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course
operating costs.
Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime
above.
Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.
Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and
records are fictional.
1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the
indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including
DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly
searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific
disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent,
payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.
2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause
11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final
written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.
3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2.
As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security
is included.
4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of
every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of
non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.
5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject
to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft
Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or
on-costs apply.
6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external
email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity
timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised
person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation
remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no
loss amount.
7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as
a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.
8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each
(AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether
each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.
9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale
consent is required merely because shares are sold.
10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of
the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the
Buyer has completed its own verification.
11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer
must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer-side review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter

**Overall view:** The package is not "fair and balanced". Read together, the limitation regime (Cl 8.3, 9.3, 12, 13, 20.5), the general data-room disclosure and the "all Claims" language would leave Wattlebridge with almost no effective recourse, while three items that go directly to the AUD 24m debt-free/cash-free price (Riverlark, the closing bonuses, Ironquay) are pushed to the post-Completion side. The Disclosure Letter is actually more candid than the Update – it concedes, in terms, that none of the key consents/releases exist – so use it against the Update.

---

## A. Price / value-leakage issues (highest priority – these move money)

### 1. Riverlark facility (Cl 2 / 7) – AUD ~3.2m
- **Departure:** Debt-free/cash-free deal, but the facility is unpaid and the Seller offers only "a release to be provided following Completion". DD-003 also has a change-of-control event (8.1) – Completion itself will likely trigger a default.
- **Why it matters:** Unless repaid at Completion from Seller's proceeds, Wattlebridge pays AUD 24m for a company carrying AUD 3.2m of debt and (probably) registered security over Company assets – and possibly over the shares themselves.
- **Push back:** Repayment at Completion out of the purchase price via funds flow; delivery at Completion of a payout letter, deed of release, PPSR discharge and any share-security release as Completion deliverables; Riverlark's consent/waiver under 8.1 obtained pre-Completion. No "following Completion".

### 2. Closing bonuses (DD-005) – AUD 420k plus on-costs
- **Departure:** Triggered by Completion but excluded from the funds flow as "a matter for the Seller". The obligor is the Company, so post-Completion the cost sits with the Buyer.
- **Why it matters:** This is a transaction cost of the Seller's. Add superannuation (12%) and NSW payroll tax (~5.45%) – ~AUD 495k gross. The "continued-employment" conditions also suggest some may crystallise after Completion, i.e. on Buyer's watch.
- **Push back:** Treat as Transaction Expenses/Debt-like items deducted from price (grossed up for on-costs), or paid by Seller through payroll at Completion. Specific indemnity for any shortfall. Obtain the bonus letters and confirm who bears retention-period payments.

### 3. Ironquay SOW3 IP (Cl 11.1 / DD-004 / DD-010) – AUD 180k open
- **Departure:** Under DD-004 cl 7.3 the Project Materials don't transfer until every SOW3 fee is paid. AUD 180k is recorded as open; no receipt or assignment in the data room. Seller's indemnity is capped at the SOW3 payment.
- **Why it matters:** This is a *title to IP* problem, not a AUD 180k problem. If the materials are core product code, the Company doesn't own what you're buying; the exposure is the business value, not the fee.
- **Push back:** Completion deliverable: evidence of cleared payment and an executed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay. Failing that, hold back/deduct AUD 180k and take a specific indemnity for all Loss arising from any defect in title to SOW3 materials – outside the basket, cap at price, long time limit. Strengthen IP ownership warranty.

### 4. Supplier renewals (DD-008 / DD-011) – 3 × AUD 110k
- **Departure:** Characterised as "ordinary course". The Disclosure Letter itself flags they should be "read together" and declines to say whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued.
- **Concern:** Three identical amounts look structured to sit under a materiality/consent threshold. If committed pre-Completion for post-Completion benefit, ask whether they are a cost of the Seller's period. Confirm whether any are already accrued (then debt-like) and ensure the pre-Completion conduct covenants require Buyer consent for commitments > a single threshold *in aggregate* with related contracts.

### 5. Bluefen consent (Cl 3 / 6.3) – ~30% of revenue
- **Departure:** Described as "addressed", but no consent exists and Seller wants (a) only reasonable endeavours and (b) the CP deemed satisfied on "delivery of the counterparty's written consent" – ignoring the cl 11.3 conditions.
- **Push back:** CP satisfied only when unconditional written consent is received (or 11.3 conditions satisfied) *in a form reasonably satisfactory to the Buyer*; Seller to use best/all reasonable endeavours; Buyer-only waiver; long-stop date with Buyer termination right; Buyer involvement in Bluefen communications. Consider a price adjustment/escrow if consent comes with amended terms.

---

## B. The limitation regime – read as a whole it eliminates recourse

### 6. Fundamental and title warranties subject to general cap/time limits
- Market position (and the only acceptable one): title, capacity, authority and (ideally) tax warranties capped at 100% of price and claimable for 6–7 years. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to accept a 20%/18-month cap on whether the Seller actually owns the shares.

### 7. "Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated" / Cl 9.3, 12.8, 20.5 apply to "all Claims of any nature"
- This sweeps specific indemnities, tax indemnity, Completion obligations (e.g. the Riverlark release), restraints, leakage and **fraud** into the caps, baskets, time limits and exclusive-remedy clause.
- **Push back:** Express carve-outs for fraud/wilful concealment, fundamental warranties, tax warranties/indemnity, specific indemnities, leakage, Completion obligations and restraint covenants. Exclusive remedy and non-reliance must not exclude claims for fraud or statutory claims that cannot be excluded (misleading or deceptive conduct under ACL s 18 cannot be contracted out of – a non-reliance clause only affects causation, so draft it accordingly and don't let the Seller suggest it is a complete shield).

### 8. General cap 20% (AUD 4.8m)
- Low for a deal without W&I insurance and with known live issues. Target 50% (or higher) for general warranties; if the Seller insists on 20%, make it conditional on a Buyer-side W&I policy with Seller contribution to premium, and keep known-issue specific indemnities outside the cap entirely.

### 9. Thresholds (Cl 12.2)
- De minimis AUD 25,000 is ~0.1% of price – acceptable to slightly high; aggregate-related claims should count together (relevant given the 3 × 110k pattern). The AUD 250,000 basket is ~1% – fine, but it should be a **tipping** basket (first dollar recoverable), not a deductible. No thresholds for fundamental, tax or specific indemnities.

### 10. Time limits (Cl 12.3 / 13)
- 18 months is short – it does not even cover two audit cycles. Push 24 months for general; 7 years for tax (ATO amendment periods); 6–7 years fundamental. Claims notified within the period should survive if proceedings commenced within 6–12 months after notification.

### 11. Buyer knowledge (Cl 8.3) – constructive knowledge
- As drafted, anything "discoverable from the data room or public records" bars a claim regardless of whether it was fairly disclosed. Combined with general disclosure, warranties become worthless. Such clauses are enforceable in NSW, so this must be negotiated, not litigated.
- **Push back:** Delete; fall-back is *actual* knowledge of a short list of named deal-team individuals, and in no case applicable to specific indemnities or fundamental warranties.

### 12. General disclosure (Schedule 7 / DL 1.1–1.2)
- Blanket disclosure of the whole data room and "publicly searchable corporate records" (undefined, undated).
- **Push back:** Only matters *fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope* of the matter qualify the warranties. Public records limited to specified ASIC, PPSR, IP Australia and court searches, dated and annexed. Fix the data-room cut-off (22 Sept) – it is stale; require a bring-down and prohibit a supplementary disclosure letter that reduces claims at Completion.

### 13. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime"
- They are not. Require a separate tax indemnity (pre-Completion tax, uncapped or capped at price, 7 years, no basket) and standalone IP ownership/non-infringement warranties, with the Ironquay indemnity above.

---

## C. Known contingent exposures needing specific protection

### 14. DD-006 export/privacy incident
- ~1,240 records of personal information sent to an unintended external recipient. The Seller calls it "preliminary, not material" and discloses it (which, on their drafting, extinguishes any warranty claim).
- Under the Privacy Act's Notifiable Data Breaches scheme the Company had 30 days from awareness to assess, and must notify OAIC and affected individuals if it is an eligible data breach; penalty exposure and the new statutory tort for serious invasions of privacy are relevant post-2024/25 reforms.
- **Push back:** Completion of the assessment and any notifications pre-Completion as a covenant/CP; specific uncapped (or price-capped) indemnity for all Loss (regulator action, notification costs, claims, Bluefen/customer contractual consequences); express statement that disclosure does not qualify the indemnity.

### 15. Title (DL 10 / DD-012)
- Seller is pointing to the Company's own register and expressly noting Buyer hasn't verified. Do our own ASIC and PPSR searches (PPSR particularly – Riverlark may have security over the shares), sight share certificates, and warrant no options/convertibles/encumbrances. Keep the title warranty fundamental and uncapped.

### 16. Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
- Lower risk, but verify the lease clause is genuinely notification-only (and give notice as a Completion step), and read DD-009's assignment restriction for any "change of control" deeming provision before accepting the Seller's reading.

---

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Buyer position |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Riverlark AUD 3.2m | Repaid at Completion from price; release/PPSR discharge/8.1 waiver are Completion deliverables |
| 2 | Closing bonuses AUD 420k + on-costs | Deducted from price or paid by Seller at Completion; indemnity |
| 3 | Ironquay SOW3 IP | Proof of payment + confirmatory assignment at Completion; otherwise holdback + uncapped title indemnity |
| 4 | Sandbar renewals | Treat as related; confirm accrual/terminability; aggregate for consent thresholds |
| 5 | Bluefen CP | Unconditional consent (11.3 satisfied), Buyer-satisfactory form, best endeavours, Buyer-only waiver, long-stop |
| 6 | Fundamental/title/tax warranties | 100% of price, 6–7 years, no basket |
| 7 | "All Claims" limitations / exclusive remedy / non-reliance | Carve out fraud, fundamental, tax, specific indemnities, leakage, Completion obligations, restraints |
| 8 | General cap 20% | Seek 50%+ or W&I-backed structure |
| 9 | Thresholds | Tipping basket; aggregate related claims; none for fundamental/tax/indemnities |
| 10 | Time limits | 24 months general; 7 years tax; 6–7 years fundamental |
| 11 | Cl 8.3 knowledge | Delete, or actual knowledge of named individuals only; never for indemnities |
| 12 | General disclosure | "Fairly disclosed" standard; defined, dated searches; no last-minute supplementary disclosure |
| 13 | Tax/IP | Standalone tax indemnity and IP warranties |
| 14 | DD-006 incident | Assessment/notification pre-Completion; specific indemnity unaffected by disclosure |
| 15 | Title | Independent ASIC/PPSR verification; warranty of no encumbrances/options |
| 16 | Lease / Mossvale | Verify clauses; notification as Completion step |

**Negotiating note:** Lead with items 1–3 and 6–7 – they are both the most commercially significant and the hardest for the Seller to defend as "market". The Disclosure Letter's own admissions (no Bluefen consent, no Riverlark discharge, bonuses not in funds flow, no Ironquay assignment) are the best evidence that the Update's characterisations ("addressed", "adequate", "ordinary course") are not supportable.

*This is a deal-team working analysis, not a substitute for formal legal sign-off by your NSW-admitted solicitors.*
